title: Getting around town
objectives: Use motion verbs: umuwi, lumabas, sumakay, bumaba, lumiko, dumiretso
Meet the locative -an verbs (puntahan, balikan) and contrast them with pumunta sa
Give commands with -um-/mag- and -in forms, and make polite requests with paki-

grammar.title: Puntahan vs pumunta sa: focusing on the place
grammar.explanation:
You know the third verb family is coming when you remember the third marker. Actor focus puts the doer in the ang-slot; object focus (-in) puts the thing there. The -an family puts the PLACE (or the person you go to) in the ang-slot.

Same event, two ways, again:

Pumunta ako sa palengke. (actor focus) — I went to the market.
Pinuntahan ko ang palengke. (locative focus) — I went to the market (that specific market we're talking about).

With puntahan, the destination graduates from a sa-phrase to the ang-phrase, and the actor drops to ng-form (ko) — exactly the same flip you learned with -in verbs. The aspects also work the same: pinuntahan (completed), pinupuntahan (incompleted), pupuntahan (contemplated).

Balikan works alike: 'Babalikan kita' — I'll come back for you. 'Binalikan niya ang nakalimutan niyang cellphone' — he went back for the phone he forgot. Use these -an verbs when the place or person is specific and central to the point — very often with people: 'Puntahan mo si Lola' — go to Grandma.

examples.tl: Pumunta kami sa bagong mall. / Pinuntahan namin ang bagong mall.
examples.en: We went to a new mall. / We went to the new mall (the specific one).

examples.tl: Babalikan ko ang bag ko sa opisina.
examples.en: I'll go back for my bag at the office.

grammar.title: Commands: basic form + ka / -in form + mo
grammar.explanation:
Tagalog commands use the verb's basic (infinitive) form — no aspect marking.

Actor-focus command: basic form + ang-pronoun with linker. 'Lumiko ka sa kanan' — turn right. 'Maglakad kayo nang diretso' — walk straight (plural/polite kayo). Softened with na or po: 'Umupo po kayo' — please sit.

Object-focus command: -in form + ng-pronoun. 'Kainin mo ito' — eat this. 'Buksan mo ang pinto' — open the door. 'Sundan ninyo ako' — follow me (ninyo for plural/polite).

Negative commands, as you learned, take huwag: 'Huwag kang lumiko dito', 'Huwag mong kalimutan!' (Don't forget it!).

In directions you will constantly hear the actor-focus commands: Dumiretso ka. Lumiko ka sa kaliwa sa kanto. Tumawid ka sa tulay. Bumaba ka sa tapat ng simbahan (get off across from the church).

examples.tl: Dumiretso ka, tapos lumiko ka sa kanan sa kanto.
examples.en: Go straight, then turn right at the corner.

examples.tl: Sumakay kayo ng dyip papuntang Cubao.
examples.en: Take a jeepney bound for Cubao.

examples.tl: Buksan mo ang mapa sa cellphone mo.
examples.en: Open the map on your phone.

examples.tl: Huwag kang bumaba sa unang kanto; sa pangalawa.
examples.en: Don't get off at the first corner; at the second one.

grammar.title: Paki-: the polite request prefix
grammar.explanation:
For requests to strangers, elders, or anyone you'd rather not boss around, Tagalog has the wonderfully handy prefix paki- ('please...'). Attach it to the verb root; the thing acted on takes ang (or stays a plain noun), and mo/po are optional garnish:

Pakisara ang pinto. — Please close the door.
Pakiabot po ang asin. — Please pass the salt.
Pakiulit po. — Please repeat that (a lifesaver for learners!).
Paki-check mo ang address. — Please check the address (yes, Manila speech happily borrows roots).

Compare bluntness levels: 'Isara mo ang pinto!' (do it), 'Pakisara ang pinto' (please), 'Puwede po bang pakisara ang pinto?' (extra polite). On jeepneys you'll hear the classic 'Pakiabot po ng bayad' — please pass the fare along — since passengers hand coins down the row to the driver. And to stop the jeepney, call out 'Para po!'

examples.tl: Pakiabot po ng bayad. — Salamat po.
examples.en: Please pass my fare. — Thank you.

examples.tl: Pakiulit po. Hindi ko po naintindihan.
examples.en: Please say it again. I didn't understand.
Please open the window. It's so hot!

examples.tl: Para po! Sa tabi lang po.
examples.en: Stop please! Just at the side (I'll get off here).

example.tl: Pupuntahan kita mamaya sa bahay.
example.en: I'll come to your place later.

example.tl: Binalikan ko ang wallet ko sa restawran.
example.en: I went back for my wallet at the restaurant.

example.tl: Uuwi ako nang maaga ngayon.
example.en: I'm going home early today.

example.tl: Lumabas siya ng bahay nang alas-otso.
example.en: He left the house at eight.

vocab.note: sumakay, sumasakay, sasakay; sumakay ng dyip

example.tl: Sumakay kami ng bus papuntang Baguio.
example.en: We took a bus to Baguio.

example.tl: Bumaba kayo sa may simbahan.
example.en: Get off near the church.

example.tl: Lumiko ka sa kaliwa pagkatapos ng tulay.
example.en: Turn left after the bridge.

example.tl: Dumiretso lang kayo hanggang sa kanto.

example.tl: Dadaan ako sa tindahan bago umuwi.
example.en: I'll pass by the store before going home.

example.tl: Maglakad na lang tayo. Malapit lang naman.
example.en: Let's just walk. It's close anyway.

example.tl: Pakisara po ang pinto.
example.en: Please close the door.

example.tl: Nasa kanan ang botika.
example.en: The pharmacy is on the right.

example.tl: Lumiko kami sa kaliwa sa kanto.
example.en: We turned left at the corner.

example.tl: May 7-Eleven sa kanto.

example.tl: Anong kalye ito?

example.tl: Alam mo ba ang daan papunta sa istasyon?

example.tl: Tumawid ka sa tulay, mas ligtas.

example.tl: Nasaan ang hintuan ng bus?
example.en: Where is the bus stop?

example.en: The MRT station is near the office.

dialogue.title: Looking for the pharmacy
dialogue.context: A visitor, Tom, asks a vendor for directions to a pharmacy in a Manila neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.tl: Magandang hapon po. Puwede po bang magtanong?
lines.en: Good afternoon. May I ask a question?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.tl: Naliligaw po yata ako. Saan po ang pinakamalapit na botika?
lines.en: I think I'm lost. Where's the nearest pharmacy?

lines.speaker: Tindera
lines.tl: Ah, madali lang. Dumiretso ka sa kalyeng ito hanggang sa kanto.
lines.en: Ah, it's easy. Go straight on this street until the corner.

lines.speaker: Tindera
lines.tl: Sa kanto, lumiko ka sa kanan. May simbahan doon. Nasa tapat ng simbahan ang botika.
lines.en: At the corner, turn right. There's a church there. The pharmacy is across from the church.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.tl: Malayo po ba? Kailangan ko po bang sumakay?
lines.en: Is it far? Do I need to take a ride?

lines.speaker: Tindera
lines.tl: Hindi na. Maglakad ka lang, mga limang minuto lang.
lines.en: No need. Just walk, only about five minutes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.tl: Pakiulit lang po? Dumiretso, tapos kanan sa kanto?
lines.en: Could you repeat that please? Straight, then right at the corner?

lines.speaker: Tindera
lines.tl: Tama! Huwag kang tatawid sa malaking kalye, ha? Nasa gilid na ito ng simbahan.
lines.en: Correct! Don't cross the big street, okay? It's on this side, by the church.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.tl: Maraming salamat po! Babalikan ko po kayo mamaya, bibili ako ng mangga ninyo.
lines.en: Thank you very much! I'll come back to you later, I'll buy some of your mangoes.

exercises.prompt: 'Pumunta ako sa palengke' vs 'Pinuntahan ko ang palengke'. What changed?
choices: The event: one is past, one is future
The focus: the place moved into the ang-slot
exercises.explain: Both report the same trip. Puntahan is a locative-focus verb, so the destination takes ang and the actor drops to ko.

exercises.prompt: Which is the contemplated (future) form of puntahan?
exercises.explain: Pupuntahan = will go to (somewhere specific). Pinuntahan is completed, pinupuntahan incompleted, pumupunta is the actor-focus verb.

exercises.prompt: Lumiko ___ sa kanan sa kanto. (Turn right at the corner.)
exercises.explain: Actor-focus commands use the basic verb form plus the ang-pronoun: lumiko ka (or polite lumiko kayo/po kayo).

exercises.prompt: Make this request polite with paki-: 'Close the door.'
exercises.explain: Paki- attaches straight to the root: pakisara (ang pinto). Add po for extra politeness.

exercises.prompt: ___ po! Sa tabi lang po. (Stop please! Just here at the side — said to a jeepney driver.)
exercises.explain: Para po! is how passengers tell the jeepney or bus driver to stop.

exercises.tl: Dumiretso ka hanggang sa kanto, tapos lumiko ka sa kaliwa. Nasa kanan ang bangko.
choices: Straight ahead, then left; the bank is on the right
Straight ahead, then right; the bank is on the left
Across the bridge on the left
exercises.explain: Dumiretso hanggang sa kanto (straight to the corner), lumiko sa kaliwa (turn left), nasa kanan ang bangko (bank on the right).

exercises.prompt: Sumakay kami ___ dyip papuntang Quiapo. (We rode a jeepney to Quiapo.)
exercises.explain: The vehicle after sumakay takes ng: sumakay ng dyip, ng bus, ng traysikel.

exercises.prompt: You left your phone at a restaurant. 'I'll go back for my phone' is:
exercises.explain: Balikan focuses the thing you return for: babalikan ko (contemplated) ang cellphone ko.

exercises.prompt: Get off in front of the church.
exercises.answer: Bumaba ka sa tapat ng simbahan.
accept: Bumaba ka sa tapat ng simbahan
Bumaba kayo sa tapat ng simbahan
Bumaba po kayo sa tapat ng simbahan
exercises.explain: Bumaba = get off; sa tapat ng = in front of / across from.

exercises.prompt: Dadaan ako sa tindahan bago umuwi.
exercises.answer: I'll pass by the store before going home.
accept: I'll pass by the store before going home
I will pass by the store before going home
I'll stop by the store before going home
I'll drop by the store before I go home
exercises.explain: Dadaan (contemplated of dumaan) = will pass by; bago + basic form umuwi = before going home.

exercises.prompt: Which command tells someone NOT to cross here?
exercises.explain: Negative commands need huwag + linked pronoun: huwag kang tumawid. Hindi negates statements, not commands.

exercises.prompt: Please repeat that. I didn't understand.
exercises.answer: Pakiulit po. Hindi ko po naintindihan.
accept: Pakiulit po. Hindi ko po naintindihan
Pakiulit po, hindi ko po naintindihan
exercises.explain: Pakiulit (po) is the essential learner's request; hindi ko naintindihan = I didn't understand it.

exercises.prompt: 'Pupuntahan kita mamaya.' Who is going where?
choices: You are coming to me later
I am coming to you later
exercises.explain: Kita fuses 'I (actor) + you (focus)': I will go to you — with puntahan, the person visited is the focus.

exercises.tl: Sumakay kayo ng dyip sa kanto, tapos bumaba kayo sa may istasyon ng MRT.
choices: Walk to the corner and cross at the station
Take a jeepney at the corner and get off near the MRT station
Take a tricycle to the church
Ride the MRT and get off at the corner
exercises.explain: Sumakay ng dyip sa kanto = board a jeepney at the corner; bumaba sa may istasyon ng MRT = get off near the MRT station.
